title: Carbon planning
excerpt: Use traceable site, species and management assumptions to compare carbon projections without confusing planning with certification.
sections: The planning question
How do alternative agroforestry designs change the timing and distribution of projected biomass and carbon while remaining workable for farmers and project teams?
How FarmTree supports the work
FarmTree connects site information, species characteristics and management choices to time-based carbon, production and economic projections. The assumptions remain visible for review.
Evidence boundaries
Modelled carbon is a projection, not a verified credit or guaranteed outcome. Applicable standards, baseline requirements, field measurement, validation and verification remain separate.
A practical workflow
Define the project boundary, compare a limited set of credible designs, review sensitivity, document data gaps and take the preferred scenario into field and specialist review.

title: Farm value modelling
excerpt: Compare costs, labour, yields and revenues over time so farmer value remains visible in project design.
sections: The planning question
Can a proposed agroforestry design create a credible path through establishment costs, changing labour needs and delayed tree-product revenues?
How FarmTree supports the work
FarmTree brings production, cost, revenue and labour assumptions into the same time-based scenario, helping teams see cash-flow timing and trade-offs.
Evidence boundaries
Prices, yields and adoption conditions can change. Results are scenario evidence rather than financial advice, assurance or a guarantee of farmer income.
A practical workflow
Agree representative farm types, document source assumptions, compare alternatives and sensitivities, then review the design with farmers and local specialists before implementation.

title: Cocoa scenario planning and monitoring
excerpt: Compare shade-tree density, species mix, renewal timing and farmer-value trade-offs before scaling a cocoa programme.
sections: The planning question
Which regenerative cocoa design can balance production continuity, shade, diversified value, labour and long-term resilience in a specific context?
How FarmTree supports the work
FarmTree compares cocoa and shade-tree arrangements using site, management, species and price assumptions, then links representative farm designs to wider programme questions.
Evidence boundaries
A representative scenario is not a measured outcome for every farm. Local calibration, farmer participation and field monitoring are required.
A practical workflow
Capture the baseline, co-design a focused set of systems, review short- and long-term trade-offs, select indicators and update scenarios as field information improves.

title: Water and landscape resilience monitoring
excerpt: Connect hydrology, erosion, land cover and farm-value questions in a transparent landscape planning process.
sections: The planning question
Where can tree-based interventions support water and landscape objectives without creating unsupported expectations about hydrological outcomes?
How FarmTree supports the work
FarmTree can compare water-balance, erosion, production, carbon and economic indicators across defined scenarios and locations.
Evidence boundaries
Hydrological responses are context-dependent. Model results require appropriate source data, calibration, uncertainty communication and field evidence.
A practical workflow
Define the catchment decision, select representative land-use systems, compare interventions, identify sensitive assumptions and connect the preferred plan to a proportionate monitoring design.
